# Lint lane-state terminals for fresh gate evidence

## Context

Operator feedback on 2026-06-20 surfaced the same neomjs/neo#10777 failure class in two active peers: a wake/FYI message was correctly classified as low-action, but the turn then ended without asking the second question: "do I have an active lane, or did I verify that no lane exists?"

Fresh anchors:

- Vega ended reactive on stale gates: PR neomjs/neo#13568 was already merged and follow-up neomjs/neo#13570 was open/assigned.
- Ada independently reported the same failure: neomjs/neo#13561 and neomjs/neo#13567 were cited as "at the merge gate" even though both had already merged.
- Ada's neomjs/neo#10777 peer-role comment (`IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABG3UdYg`) converges on the two-phase `wakeDisposition` / `laneContinuation` split and adds three refinements: `awaiting-own-PR` is not active-lane, named gates need same-turn `checkedAt`, and `verified-no-lane` needs a full backlog survey.

Release classification: boardless (Agent OS stability follow-up; not release-blocking unless the operator explicitly boards it).

Duplicate sweep: live latest-open sweep at 2026-06-20T00:25Z found neomjs/neo#10777 as the source family and neomjs/neo#12612/#12633/#11829 as broader wake-driver enforcement work, but no narrow terminal-evidence lint ticket. A2A recency sweep at 2026-06-20T00:25Z found Ada's neomjs/neo#10777 peer-role comment and no competing lane-claim for this exact leaf.

## The Problem

The current substrate says the right thing, but agents can still launder idling through disciplined-sounding terminal prose:

- `wakeDisposition=awareness|stale` answers only whether to engage the message; it does not answer whether the turn has an active lane.
- `awaiting-own-PR` on merge/review/CI is a background watch, not `active-lane`.
- A terminal that names an issue or PR gate can be stale unless it cites same-turn live evidence.
- `verified-no-lane` can collapse into an own-PR or own-epic slice instead of a named full-backlog survey.

This has recurred despite neomjs/neo#13197, the current `/post-review-pickup` wording, and multiple memories. More prose alone is losing to rationalization.

## The Architectural Reality

The source-of-authority family is neomjs/neo#10777. The operative substrate already includes:

- `.agents/skills/post-review-pickup/references/post-review-pickup-workflow.md`: lifecycle cycle, `lane-state:` boundary, PR-state freshness gate, and no generic idle terminal.
- `.agents/skills/peer-role/references/peer-role-mode.md`: stale-wake silent-mark-read anti-pattern.
- `ai/daemons/wake/wakeLaneDirective.mjs`: narrowed hard never-idle directive after neomjs/neo#13197.

This ticket is deliberately smaller than neomjs/neo#12633. neomjs/neo#12633 is the deferred external liveness enforcement layer that independently computes claimable work through deployment-aware state. This ticket only validates the evidence shape of an agent-authored turn-terminal claim so stale gate names and own-slice `verified-no-lane` claims are mechanically rejected.

## The Fix

Add a focused terminal-evidence lint/check on the existing Agent OS lint/tooling surface chosen during implementation intake. The checker should validate machine-readable or conventionally structured `lane-state` / turn-terminal text in lifecycle artifacts (final responses, A2A lifecycle handoffs, or the selected persisted turn-boundary surface) without becoming a contribution counter.

Rules to encode:

1. `wakeDisposition=awareness|stale|suppressed` is not a turn terminal unless paired with `laneContinuation`.
2. `laneContinuation=active-lane` explicitly excludes `awaiting-own-PR` states: own PR waiting on merge, review, or CI resolves to `next-lane` unless the author has concrete work on that PR.
3. Any terminal that names a PR or issue gate must cite a same-turn `checkedAt` for each named artifact.
4. `verified-no-lane` must cite a named full-backlog survey artifact (`list_issues`, `gh issue list`, or equivalent) with `checkedAt` and a considered-lanes summary. Own-PR-only or own-epic-only surveys fail.
5. Valid `next-lane`, `blocker-routed`, and active implementation/review states must pass without requiring backlog survey noise.

If implementation modifies `.agents/skills/**`, follow Progressive Disclosure: keep always-loaded/router deltas minimal, move rule body into the relevant payload or lint docs, and include the `/turn-memory-pre-flight` load-effect audit in the PR body.

## Decision Record Impact

None. This is aligned with neomjs/neo#10777 and the neomjs/neo-agent-brain#148/#12630 lineage, while explicitly avoiding the deferred neomjs/neo#12633 external-enforcement scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A focused lint/check exists for turn-terminal evidence shape in the chosen Agent OS lifecycle artifact surface.
- [ ] Tests fail a stale named gate without same-turn `checkedAt`.
- [ ] Tests fail `active-lane` when the only cited lane is `awaiting-own-PR` on merge/review/CI.
- [ ] Tests fail `verified-no-lane` when the evidence is only an own-PR/own-epic slice and lacks a named full-backlog survey.
- [ ] Tests pass valid `next-lane`, `blocker-routed`, active review/implementation, and `verified-no-lane` with a named backlog survey.
- [ ] The PR documents why the implementation is not a contribution counter, FAIR band, central assignment mechanism, or neomjs/neo#12633 external claimability engine.
- [ ] If `.agents/skills/**` changes, the source ticket carries the Contract Ledger and the PR body carries the load-effect audit required by the skill substrate gate.

## Out of Scope

- Full external liveness enforcement / Stop-hook behavior from neomjs/neo#12633.
- Provider-backed claimability computation across GitHub/GitLab/cloud tenants.
- Contribution counting, PR quotas, FAIR bands, scoreboards, or central lane assignment.
- Changing the human-only merge rule.

* feat(ai): dry-run Stop-hook scaffold for idle-out enforcement (#12633)

Neo's first Claude Code Stop hook (.claude/hooks/laneStateStopHook.mjs) — DRY-RUN/log-only by default. Per the Option-A convergence: reads the turn transcript, validates the lane-state terminal, and in ENFORCING mode (operator-gated via NEO_LANE_STATE_ENFORCE) blocks the stop + injects a pick-a-lane directive on an invalid idle-out. * feat(ai): integrate the lane-state seam spec into the Stop-hook 3-bucket chain (#12633)

Integrates ada's delivered seam spec — the fenced lane-state emission + parseLaneState(text) -> descriptor|null|throw + validateLaneStateTerminal -> {valid, violations}. The hook chain now distinguishes three buckets via the pure exported parseOutcomeToVerdict: absent (null), malformed (parseLaneState throws — the agent's garbage, a real block-able bucket), and descriptor -> validate. Read-failure (ours -> allow) is cleanly separated from a parse-throw, and a validator throw also allows (never block on our own bug). parseLaneState + validateLaneStateTerminal stay signature-accurate stubs for ada's bodies to drop in. 7 unit tests (4 chain buckets + 3 decision paths) pass.

* feat(ai): wire the lane-state parser+validator into the Stop-hook + e2e falsification (#12633)

Folds ada's pure parseLaneState + validateLaneStateTerminal modules (ai/scripts/lifecycle, cherry-picked from agent/13575) into the hook as the real seam, replacing the stubs — the hook imports them (zero-dependency, stays light on every turn-end). Adds the end-to-end falsification test: spawns the real hook with real lane-state emissions (valid / invalid / absent / malformed + the enforcing block path) and asserts the wired parser+validator fire through the hook I/O. Block path drains stdout before exit (no truncation). 12 tests pass (7 pure + 5 e2e). Per Euclid's #13577 CR the validator lands WITH the firing caller, so #13577 supersedes into this PR; #13575 + #12633 converge into the one wiring-first deliverable.

* fix(ai): read last_assistant_message (+ JSONL fallback) for the Stop-hook lane-state, not raw transcript (#12633)

Addresses the #13589 CR (input boundary mismatch): the hook scanned transcript_path as raw Markdown, but Claude's Stop input provides last_assistant_message (the decoded final message carrying the lane-state block), and raw JSONL is escaped so parseLaneState(rawLine) returns null -> a valid terminal logged a false WOULD-BLOCK. Now extractFinalAssistantText reads last_assistant_message first (string or message object), falling back to JSONL-parsing transcript_path for the last assistant record's text; the fence parser only runs on extracted text. Regression coverage: real Stop payload shape + JSONL fallback shape + resolver units. 18 tests pass.
